dataflow.outcome: local availability loss or command failure for one KCS process and selected scope
dataflow.sink: `fs::read()` whole-file allocation and SHA-256 hashing inside `find_working_tree_raw()`
dataflow.source: attacker-sized direct-child regular files plus a caller-supplied absent or late-matching raw hash

finalSeverity.why: The scan's mandatory matrix maps Medium impact and Medium likelihood to Low/P3.

impact.why: The resource sink can make a local KCS command slow, memory pressured, or unavailable, but it does not by itself disclose data, execute code, or persistently corrupt state.

likelihood.why: The path is reachable from normal read-oriented commands in a hostile scope, but it requires operator invocation and is not exposed as a public background service.

limitations: The effect is transient and recoverable by removing the hostile file or avoiding the supplied pointer.
No unsafe large allocation or sparse-file stress test was run.
The prevalence of automatically consumed attacker-supplied Evidence Pointers is unknown.

reachability.access_requirements: file-content control in the selected scope; no private `.kcs` write, credentials, administrator access, or shell access to the victim process
reachability.attacker: lower-trust contributor to an adopted/shared scope
reachability.outcome: the victim process incurs O(max n_i) peak input allocation and O(sum n_i) I/O/hash work
preconditions: the selected scope contains attacker-controlled large or sparse direct-child regular files
the requested raw hash is absent or late in directory enumeration
host resource limits are low enough relative to the candidate file size for visible degradation
reachability.summary: The attacker needs file-content control in an operator-selected scope and a raw-object resolution. KCS has no public listener for this path, and the operator still invokes the local command.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust content contributor places one or more very large or sparse regular direct-child files in a scope the operator uses. When the operator or automation resolves an absent or late-matching raw hash through open, view, or Evidence, KCS reads and hashes each candidate before CAS lookup, causing local CPU, disk I/O, and memory pressure in the victim process.

category: uncontrolled local resource consumption / denial of service

codeEvidence.explanation: `open` and `view` carry caller-supplied raw object identifiers or Evidence Pointer text into the resolver. This is the attacker-influenced trigger once the operator runs the local command in a lower-trust scope.
codeEvidence.label: open and view accept caller-supplied raw hashes or pointers

codeEvidence.explanation: After pointer validation, the saved `raw_hash` is forwarded to `open_raw_object()`. The lower-trust scope's files become lookup candidates for the victim process.
codeEvidence.label: Evidence Pointer resolution reaches raw-object lookup

codeEvidence.explanation: `open_raw_object()` sets `scan_working_tree` to true, and `open_cas_byte_object()` scans the working tree before checking whether the requested raw object already exists in CAS.
codeEvidence.label: working-tree scan runs before CAS lookup

codeEvidence.explanation: The nearest controls skip `.kcs` and non-files, but every remaining regular file is allocated in full before hashing. There is no metadata size precheck, streaming reader, aggregate byte budget, or indexed lookup.
codeEvidence.label: each regular direct child is read wholly and hashed

remediation.invariant: Raw-object lookup must not allocate or hash attacker-controlled scope content without explicit per-file and aggregate budgets.
regression_tests: absent raw hash in a scope with multiple direct-child regular files
existing CAS raw object while unrelated working-tree files are present
direct-child file larger than the per-file limit
many small files whose aggregate size exceeds the scan budget
`.kcs`, directories, symlinks, and special files remain excluded
remediation.summary: Hash working-tree candidates through a bounded streaming reader or an indexed raw-hash lookup. Apply per-file and aggregate byte/work ceilings, and avoid scanning unrelated working-tree files before a verified CAS hit when rename tolerance is not required.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that raw-object resolution should bound work to the requested object or an explicit lookup budget. The implementation performs rename-tolerant working-tree discovery first and uses whole-file allocation for every eligible direct child, so unrelated lower-trust scope files can control memory, disk I/O, and CPU cost before CAS is consulted.

summary: Raw-object open, view, and Evidence workflows scan the selected scope's direct-child files before checking the immutable CAS store. Each regular file is allocated in full with fs::read() and then hashed, so a lower-trust contributor to an adopted scope can force O(max n_i) live input allocation and O(sum n_i) I/O and CPU work for an absent or late-matching raw hash.
title: Raw-hash working-tree resolution reads every direct child without bounds

assertions: Peak retained input allocation is proportional to the largest visited file.
Total read and hash work is proportional to the sum of all visited eligible files for an absent or late-matching hash.
The configured adapter `max_input_bytes` does not govern this read-oriented resolver.
limitations: Peak RSS and sparse-file behavior were intentionally not stress-tested.
Directory order and host resource limits determine the exact failure point.
validation.method: V5 bounded resource analysis plus V10 exact static caller trace
validation.summary: Static source tracing confirms that open, view, and Evidence paths can call `find_working_tree_raw()`, that the scan runs before CAS lookup, and that each eligible regular file is fully read and hashed. The saved bounded control used only 98,304 total synthetic bytes and intentionally avoided unsafe stress testing.
